title: All-Inclusive in Biograd na Moru 2027: Prices & Options
metaDescription: Is there all-inclusive in Biograd na Moru? Yes, Family Hotel Adria. Prices per person, what's included, half-board vs apartment, and who it suits.
content:
## Is there all-inclusive in Biograd na Moru?

Yes, but the choice is narrow. Family Hotel Adria (Augusta Šenoe 42) is the only hotel in town that is clearly sold as all-inclusive. It is a 4-star property with about 209 rooms, set in a pine forest. The hotel is about 300–350 m from the sandy Soline beach and roughly 800 m from the town centre. Other Biograd hotels, such as those in the Ilirija Resort, are mostly sold on half-board or full-board.

There is no large multi-pool resort with a wristband system in Biograd. Anyone who wants a full resort format has to look at nearby towns.

## What does all-inclusive at Hotel Adria include?

- Buffet breakfast, lunch and dinner, with drinks at meals (soft drinks, juice, water, beer, house wine).
- An all-inclusive bar by the outdoor pool, open about 10:00–23:00, with beer, wine, soft drinks, juices and coffee. Some price lists also mention a selection of cocktails and spirits.
- An afternoon snack, such as ice cream and coffee at around 16:00–17:00.
- Outdoor pools, Wi-Fi, and kids' animation in season.

Extras usually cost more: the spa and massages, premium drinks, excursions to Krka, Kornati or Plitvice, and parking at roughly €10–12 per day. A tourist tax of about €1.50–3 per person per night is paid on site, depending on the season and the booking.

## How much does all-inclusive cost per person per night?

Prices swing widely by date and by booking channel. These are rough figures based on current 2026 package pricing, converted to per-person-per-night for two adults:

- **Peak (late July to late August):** about €125–180. A 7-night promotional package for two in summer is around €1,780. Mid-August family packages with children staying free reach about €2,500 for 7 nights, which is about €180 per adult per night.
- **Shoulder (June, early September, late September):** about €90–100. A September 3-night package for two is around €560, or about €93 per person per night. Weekly offers from tour operators in this period come to about €96.
- **Late autumn:** short breaks can fall below €70 per person per night.

All-inclusive here is not a budget product. The cheapest nights are in autumn, and the best-value promotions include two children free.

## All-inclusive vs half-board vs private apartment

The half-board and apartment figures below are estimates for Biograd, not fixed hotel tariffs. They vary by property.

| Option | Peak, per person/night | Shoulder, per person/night |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive (Hotel Adria) | €125–180 | €90–100 |
| Half-board (Biograd hotels, estimate) | €75–110 | €50–70 |
| Private apartment, self-catering (estimate) | €20–35 for the room, plus about €30–45 food and drink | €15–25 for the room, plus about €25–35 food and drink |

An apartment with groceries and one restaurant dinner every two or three days usually works out at €50–80 per person per night in peak season. That is roughly half the all-inclusive price. The gap narrows only when drinks are heavy or several children are in the group.

## Who suits all-inclusive in Biograd?

**Families with small children.** Meals at fixed times, a pool, kids' animation, and no cooking or dishes make it easy. Children's reductions and free-child offers can cut the price per person sharply. Soline beach is a short walk, which helps with strollers.

**Short stays of 2–4 nights.** Packages for two nights in autumn start around €180 per person. The convenience outweighs the premium, and there is no grocery shopping or planning.

**Guests who drink beer and wine at lunch and dinner.** Drinks at meals and at the bar are included, so the package pays back faster.

## Who should self-cater?

- **Stays of a week or longer.** Variety matters, and eating at the same buffet gets repetitive.
- **Couples and groups of adults who want to eat out.** Biograd's harbour has many restaurants, and a fish dinner for two costs about €50–80.
- **Travellers without small children.** The hotel's animation and family focus can feel busy in August.
- **Anyone wanting day trips.** Lunch is already paid for at the hotel, so exploring Vransko Lake, Kornati or Pašman by boat becomes a double cost.

For a 7-night adult-only peak-season trip, an apartment is the better choice. For a family with children under 12, all-inclusive at Adria is competitive, especially with the free-child offers.

## Nearest all-inclusive alternatives

A wider resort format needs a short drive:

- **Pakoštane (about 15 km south-east):** Pine Beach Pakoštane sells an all-inclusive light package focused on sport and nature.
- **Zadar (about 28 km north-west):** Hotel Donat offers all-inclusive from about €42 per night in low season.
- **Vodice (about 45 km south-east):** Hotel Punta Vodice and Villa Arausa sell family all-inclusive light packages.

All-inclusive light usually means meals plus drinks only with meals, rather than an open bar all day.

## Insider tips

- The hotel shows on booking sites under slightly different names. Compare the offers titled "Family Hotel Adria" and "Hotel Adria" before paying.
- Tour-operator and voucher platforms often undercut the hotel's own rates, mostly for September and October.
- Check that the all-inclusive bar hours (10:00–23:00) match what you need. Alcohol outside the bar hours is paid extra.
- If a car is not needed, skip the parking fee. The bus station and centre are about 800 m away on foot.
- Cheaper than Adria and more flexible: book a half-board room in the town centre and eat lunch at a bakery or konoba.

faq.question: Is there an all-inclusive hotel in Biograd na Moru?
faq.answer: Yes. Family Hotel Adria 4* is the only hotel in Biograd clearly sold as all-inclusive. It is about 300–350 m from Soline beach and has outdoor pools, a spa and kids' animation in season.

faq.question: How much is all-inclusive in Biograd na Moru per person?
faq.answer: Roughly €125–180 per person per night in peak summer, and about €90–100 in September and shoulder months. Autumn short breaks can be lower, and offers with children staying free reduce the per-person cost.

faq.question: What does all-inclusive include at Hotel Adria?
faq.answer: Buffet breakfast, lunch and dinner with drinks at meals, plus a pool bar open about 10:00–23:00 and an afternoon snack. Spa treatments, excursions and parking (about €10–12 per day) cost extra.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive or an apartment cheaper in Biograd?
faq.answer: An apartment is usually cheaper, at about €50–80 per person per night in peak season, including groceries and some restaurant meals. All-inclusive costs about €125–180. It wins only for families with children who stay free.

faq.question: Where is the nearest all-inclusive resort to Biograd na Moru?
faq.answer: Pakoštane (about 15 km) has Pine Beach with all-inclusive light. Zadar (about 28 km) has Hotel Donat, and Vodice (about 45 km) has Hotel Punta and Villa Arausa.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive in Biograd good for families with small children?
faq.answer: Yes. Fixed meal times, pools, kids' animation, a short walk to a sandy beach and free-child offers make it practical. It is best for stays of 3–7 nights.

quickAnswer: Yes. Biograd na Moru has one clear all-inclusive hotel, the 4-star Family Hotel Adria, 300–350 m from Soline beach. Expect roughly €90–100 per person per night in shoulder season and €125–180 in peak summer. Families with young children and short stays benefit most. Long stays and independent travellers do better self-catering.
